boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Marquette University
boards.description: Current late-hour food stops on and around Marquette’s Milwaukee campus, using university dining pages and the City of Milwaukee’s extended-hours license report.

cards.title: The Commons
cards.subtitle: 721 N 17th St, on the corner of 17th and Wells
cards.notes: Check the dining page before heading out, then use a meal swipe or purchase entry for the all-you-care-to-eat hall and its multiple stations.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus dining hall with regular service listed through 11 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette Dining lists The Commons at 721 N. 17th Street, calls it a late-night dining hall, and lists regular hours through 11:00 p.m.
cards.source_title: The Commons | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Regular hours are listed through 11:00 p.m.; the page also posts special hours, so confirm the date before visiting.

cards.title: Schroeder Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: 725 N 13th St, Marquette campus
cards.notes: Use the current dining schedule to time a weekday dinner stop; one listed meal option includes a drink with a swipe during the meal period.
cards.short_summary: A campus dining hall whose Monday–Thursday dinner runs to 10 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette Dining lists Schroeder Dining Hall at 725 N. 13th St. and regular Monday–Thursday dinner hours of 4:30–10:00 p.m.
cards.source_title: Schroeder Dining Hall | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Regular Monday–Thursday dinner is listed until 10:00 p.m.; Friday and weekend service ends earlier, and special closures are posted.

cards.title: Real Chili on West Wells
cards.subtitle: 1625 W Wells St, beside campus
cards.notes: Use the West Wells address when checking the current extended-hours listing, and plan around the day-specific close time rather than assuming every night matches.
cards.short_summary: A licensed extended-hours food stop immediately by Marquette’s Wells Street edge.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Milwaukee’s current extended-hours license report lists Real Chili at 1625 W. Wells St. open until 2:00 a.m. Monday–Tuesday and 3:00 a.m. Wednesday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: City of Milwaukee Extended Hours Establishments License Report
cards.access_notes: City license report lists closing at 2:00–3:00 a.m. Monday–Saturday; Sunday is listed until 11:00 p.m.

cards.title: Papa John's Pizza on West Wells
cards.subtitle: 1611 W Wells St, beside campus
cards.notes: Confirm ordering and pickup details directly with this West Wells location, then use the city’s day-by-day closing times to plan a late food pickup.
cards.short_summary: A nearby pizza location with city-licensed hours as late as 3 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Milwaukee’s current extended-hours license report lists Papa John’s Pizza at 1611 W. Wells St. open until 2:00 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: City of Milwaukee Extended Hours Establishments License Report
cards.access_notes: City license report lists service until 2:00 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Gordo's Bubble Waffles
cards.subtitle: 1633 W Wells St, beside campus
cards.notes: Save the precise Wells Street address and check the business before departure; the municipal license specifically records late Friday and Saturday availability.
cards.short_summary: A dessert-focused Wells Street stop licensed to 2 a.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Milwaukee’s current extended-hours license report lists Gordo’s Bubble Waffles at 1633 W. Wells St. with Friday and Saturday hours until 2:00 a.m.
cards.source_title: City of Milwaukee Extended Hours Establishments License Report
cards.access_notes: City license report lists Friday and Saturday service until 2:00 a.m.; verify current operating details before going.

cards.title: Domino's Pizza on West Wisconsin
cards.subtitle: 719 W Wisconsin Ave, east of campus
cards.notes: Use the West Wisconsin Avenue address for delivery or pickup details, and select a day that matches the currently licensed late closing schedule.
cards.short_summary: A downtown pizza option with licensed hours into the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Milwaukee’s current extended-hours license report lists Domino’s Pizza at 719 W. Wisconsin Ave. open until 1:00 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: City of Milwaukee Extended Hours Establishments License Report
cards.access_notes: City license report lists closing at 1:00 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: QDOBA Mexican Grill on Water Street
cards.subtitle: 1150 N Water St, downtown Milwaukee
cards.notes: Check the Water Street location’s service options first, then use the city’s day-specific times when planning a late downtown meal after campus activities.
cards.short_summary: A downtown Mexican-food option with especially late Thursday through Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Milwaukee’s current extended-hours license report lists QDOBA Mexican Grill at 1150 N. Water St. open until 3:30 a.m. Thursday and 4:30 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: City of Milwaukee Extended Hours Establishments License Report
cards.access_notes: City license report lists Thursday closing at 3:30 a.m. and Friday–Saturday closing at 4:30 a.m.; other nights end earlier.

cards.title: Real Chili on East Wells
cards.subtitle: 419 E Wells St, downtown Milwaukee
cards.notes: Use the East Wells Street address when checking current service information, and plan for the late schedule shown for Wednesday through Saturday in the city report.
cards.short_summary: A separate downtown Real Chili location licensed into the early morning on several nights.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Milwaukee’s current extended-hours license report lists Real Chili at 419 E. Wells St. open until 2:00 a.m. Wednesday, 3:30 a.m. Thursday, and 3:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: City of Milwaukee Extended Hours Establishments License Report
cards.access_notes: City license report lists late service Wednesday–Saturday, with a 3:30 a.m. close on Thursday.

cards.title: McDonald's on West Washington
cards.subtitle: 1575 W Washington St, Milwaukee
cards.notes: Confirm the location’s available ordering method before traveling from campus; the city report records exceptionally late licensed hours at this specific West Washington address.
cards.short_summary: A farther food option listed by the city as operating until 4 a.m. Monday through Thursday.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Milwaukee’s current extended-hours license report lists McDonald’s at 1575 W. Washington St. with Monday–Thursday hours of 5:00 a.m.–4:00 a.m.
cards.source_title: City of Milwaukee Extended Hours Establishments License Report
cards.access_notes: City license report lists Monday–Thursday service from 5:00 a.m. until 4:00 a.m.; confirm current service before making the trip.

cards.title: Speed Queen Bar-B-Q
cards.subtitle: 1130 W Walnut St, Milwaukee
cards.notes: Verify the day’s food service before traveling from campus, then use the current municipal schedule to choose a weeknight or weekend late meal window.
cards.short_summary: A Milwaukee barbecue restaurant with city-licensed service to 1:30 or 2 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Milwaukee’s current extended-hours license report lists Speed Queen Bar-B-Q at 1130 W. Walnut St. open until 1:30 a.m. Monday–Thursday and 2:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: City of Milwaukee Extended Hours Establishments License Report
cards.access_notes: City license report lists closing at 1:30 a.m. Monday–Thursday and 2:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Marquette spaces for individual work, group projects, creative production, reflection, and campus connection.

cards.title: Raynor Library First Floor
cards.subtitle: Raynor Library
cards.notes: Set up at the large tables when your group needs power, computers, and flexible seating; check the northeast open-classroom signage before relying on it.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative library floor built around tables, computers, outlets, and adaptable seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette identifies Raynor’s first floor as a collaborative zone with computers, large tables with power outlets, comfortable seating, and an open classroom area.
cards.source_title: Places To Study | Raynor Library | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: The northeast open classroom may be reserved for events, tutoring, or classes; consult on-site availability.

cards.title: Raynor Library Second Floor
cards.subtitle: Raynor Library
cards.notes: Use the north-end large tables for a shared session, or move south for smaller tables and whiteboards when your group needs to sketch out a plan.
cards.short_summary: One floor offers both table-and-computer work and smaller whiteboard-friendly setups.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette says Raynor’s second floor has large study tables and computers on the north end, with smaller tables and whiteboards on the south end for individual and group study.
cards.source_title: Places To Study | Raynor Library | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: This is designated a collaborative zone; keep device audio and loud conversations out of the space.

cards.title: The Bridge
cards.subtitle: Between Raynor Library and the Lemonis Center
cards.notes: Meet on the bridge when you want a central table with outlets and nearby seating; bring your own materials if you need to work outside café service periods.
cards.short_summary: A connective study spot with tables, power, and seating between two academic hubs.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette describes the Bridge, connecting Raynor and Lemonis on the second floors, as offering comfortable chairs, power outlets, and large tables.
cards.source_title: Places To Study | Raynor Library | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: The Brew @ the Bridge operates during fall and spring semesters; its food and drinks require purchase.

cards.title: Lemonis Center for Student Success
cards.subtitle: Lemonis Center, floors 2–4
cards.notes: Start at the Ask Me Desk if you need direction, then use the open study areas or reserve a technology-enabled room for a meeting, tutoring, or project session.
cards.short_summary: Academic support, career resources, study space, and reservable rooms share one student-success hub.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette states that the Lemonis Center has open study areas, a commuter lounge, technology-enhanced reservable rooms, and academic and career resources.
cards.source_title: Lemonis Center for Student Success | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Technology-enhanced rooms are reservable; use the center’s reservation process before planning a group session.

cards.title: Lemonis Stacks
cards.subtitle: Lemonis Center, lower level, 1st and 3rd–5th floors
cards.notes: Choose a table near an elevator for power, then keep conversations elsewhere: these stack levels are designated for quiet individual work rather than collaborative sessions.
cards.short_summary: Library-stack seating pairs tables and outlets with a quiet-study designation on most levels.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette says the Lemonis Stacks offer tables with power outlets and small tables, and that all listed levels except Level 2 are designated quiet zones.
cards.source_title: Places To Study | Raynor Library | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Level 2 is the collaborative exception; the other listed stack levels are quiet zones.

cards.title: Raynor Reading Rooms
cards.subtitle: Raynor Library, rooms 209 and 212
cards.notes: For a quieter solo session, head down the wide hallway toward the bridge and claim a window-side seat with access to power for an extended work block.
cards.short_summary: Two quiet rooms near the bridge combine window light, comfortable seating, and power outlets.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette identifies Raynor rooms 209 and 212 as quiet-zone reading rooms with windows, comfortable seating, and power outlets.
cards.source_title: Places To Study | Raynor Library | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Located on Raynor’s second floor in the hallway leading onto the Bridge.

cards.title: Raynor Lower Level Study Area
cards.subtitle: Raynor Library lower level
cards.notes: Use the mix of chairs, tables, and outlets for an informal study meet-up, then move into a group study room if your session needs a more contained setup.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level study area with varied seating, power, and nearby group rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette says the Raynor lower level and Beaumier Suites Conference Center lobby offer chairs, tables, power outlets, and group study rooms.
cards.source_title: Places To Study | Raynor Library | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Group rooms may be first-come, first-served unless reserved; check reservation status before settling in.

cards.title: Raynor Room R060D
cards.subtitle: Raynor Library lower level
cards.notes: Choose R060D when you need a shared place to join an online class; look at the sign outside first because events can take over the room.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level collaborative room specifically identified for students taking online classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette states that Raynor Room R060D is available for open study unless reserved and directs students taking online classes to use it.
cards.source_title: Places To Study | Raynor Library | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Open for study only when not reserved for an event; review the availability signage outside the room.

cards.title: Digital Media Editing Room
cards.subtitle: Raynor Library, room R140A
cards.notes: Reserve this room before recording an interview, narration, or group audio project; its Mac Studio and installed editing software make it suited to finishing media work on campus.
cards.short_summary: A reservation-only room for recording audio and editing video or audio projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette says Raynor’s Digital Media Editing Room has a Mac Studio, two boom-arm microphones, sound-dampened walls, and Audacity, Final Cut Pro, and Adobe Creative Cloud.
cards.source_title: Places To Study | Raynor Library | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: A reservation is required to use the room.

cards.title: Center for Engagement and Inclusion
cards.subtitle: Alumni Memorial Union, room 111
cards.notes: Drop into the CEI to connect with multicultural student organizations or use its interaction and study space; staff are available in nearby AMU 121 when needed.
cards.short_summary: An AMU space for student interaction, study, and multicultural student-organization use.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette states that the Center for Engagement and Inclusion in AMU Room 111 provides student interaction and study spaces and space for multicultural student organizations.
cards.source_title: Center for Engagement and Inclusion | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: The center is open when the Alumni Memorial Union is open; visit AMU 121 to see a staff member.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-purchase ways for Marquette students to move, make plans with friends, explore art, or join a campus gathering.

cards.title: Set up a basketball run
cards.subtitle: Rec Plex, 915 W. Wisconsin Ave.
cards.notes: Bring friends during open facility time and use one of the two gymnasiums for a casual shootaround or a small pickup game.
cards.short_summary: A gym-based meetup with room to move and play together.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rec Plex has two gymnasiums, and Marquette states that indoor recreation facilities are free to all students.
cards.source_title: Rec Plex | Campus Recreation | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Available to Marquette students at no charge; check current Rec Plex hours before going.

cards.title: Rally on a racquetball court
cards.subtitle: Rec Plex, 915 W. Wisconsin Ave.
cards.notes: Meet a friend for a racquetball session, then use the facility’s posted hours to choose a time that works for both schedules.
cards.short_summary: A quick two-person activity inside the campus recreation facility.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rec Plex includes three racquetball courts, and Marquette states that indoor recreation facilities are free to all students.
cards.source_title: Rec Plex | Campus Recreation | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Available to Marquette students at no charge; confirm facility availability before play.

cards.title: Try a squash match
cards.subtitle: Rec Plex, 915 W. Wisconsin Ave.
cards.notes: Coordinate with a friend and use the Rec Plex squash court for a short match or a beginner-friendly practice session.
cards.short_summary: A one-court racquet sport option for an active hang.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rec Plex includes one squash court, and Marquette states that indoor recreation facilities are free to all students.
cards.source_title: Rec Plex | Campus Recreation | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Available to Marquette students at no charge; ask staff about court availability.

cards.title: Walk laps and catch up
cards.subtitle: Rec Plex, 915 W. Wisconsin Ave.
cards.notes: Choose an easy pace with a friend on the suspended jogging track and turn a conversation into a low-key movement break.
cards.short_summary: A conversation-friendly indoor walk when the weather turns.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rec Plex includes a suspended jogging track, and Marquette states that indoor recreation facilities are free to all students.
cards.source_title: Rec Plex | Campus Recreation | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Available to Marquette students at no charge; use during posted Rec Plex hours.

cards.title: Do a cardio check-in
cards.subtitle: Rec Plex, 915 W. Wisconsin Ave.
cards.notes: Pick nearby machines and keep each other company through a simple cardio session using the facility’s treadmills, bikes, rowers, or ellipticals.
cards.short_summary: A flexible workout hang with several machine choices.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rec Plex offers cardio machines including treadmills, stationary bikes, rowers, and ellipticals; indoor recreation facilities are free to all students.
cards.source_title: Rec Plex | Campus Recreation | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Available to Marquette students at no charge; follow posted equipment and facility guidance.

cards.title: Lift with a workout buddy
cards.subtitle: Rec Plex, 915 W. Wisconsin Ave.
cards.notes: Bring a friend for a planned strength session in the free weight room, using spotting and equipment etiquette that fit your experience.
cards.short_summary: A structured gym session for students who prefer strength training.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rec Plex includes a free weight room, and Marquette states that indoor recreation facilities are free to all students.
cards.source_title: Rec Plex | Campus Recreation | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Available to Marquette students at no charge; use equipment safely and observe facility rules.

cards.title: Practice your golf swing
cards.subtitle: Rec Plex, 915 W. Wisconsin Ave.
cards.notes: Meet up for a focused practice break in the golf practice area, then check with recreation staff if you need guidance on access.
cards.short_summary: An indoor practice option that is different from a standard gym workout.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rec Plex includes a golf practice area, and Marquette states that indoor recreation facilities are free to all students.
cards.source_title: Rec Plex | Campus Recreation | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Available to Marquette students at no charge; check in with staff for current practice-area guidance.

cards.title: Plan a pool meetup
cards.subtitle: Wellness + Helfaer Recreation, 525 N. 16th St.
cards.notes: Coordinate a swim with friends and review pool hours before heading over, since availability can change with programming and lifeguard staffing.
cards.short_summary: A campus swim option for a group movement break.
cards.evidence_claim: Currently enrolled Marquette students have access to the pool at Wellness + Helfaer Recreation, and Marquette states its indoor recreation facilities are free to all students.
cards.source_title: Rec Plex | Campus Recreation | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Available to currently enrolled Marquette students at no charge; consult current pool hours before visiting.

cards.title: Take an art-gallery study break
cards.subtitle: Haggerty Museum of Art, 1234 W. Tory Hill St.
cards.notes: Meet at the galleries, look through the current exhibition together, and use the museum’s invitation to take a study break in the space.
cards.short_summary: Free art viewing paired with a quiet campus conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Haggerty encourages students to study or take a study break in its galleries and lists free admission.
cards.source_title: Educational Programs for University Students | Haggerty Museum of Art | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: Free admission; the museum lists Monday–Saturday hours and notes occasional installation closures.

cards.title: Join the Wednesday Ignite gathering
cards.subtitle: Lunda Room, Alumni Memorial Union, second floor
cards.notes: Drop in with a friend for conversation, reflection, and prayer; no sign-up is needed, and a free student dinner is offered most weeks.
cards.short_summary: A weekly Campus Ministry gathering centered on community and reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Ignite meets Wednesday evenings, welcomes all at Marquette, requires no sign-up, and offers students a free dinner most weeks.
cards.source_title: Ignite | Campus Ministry | Marquette University
cards.access_notes: No sign-up is necessary. The fall schedule is released in early September; free dinner is offered most weeks, not guaranteed every week.

cards.subtitle: 1355 W. Wisconsin Ave.

cards.short_summary: The main library combines study seating, computers, and group-study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette identifies Raynor Library as offering seating, computer access, and group study spaces.
cards.source_title: Raynor Library | Marquette University Campus Map
cards.access_notes: The campus map states that Raynor Library has 24-hour access; confirm current library services and policies before visiting.

cards.title: R026 Group Study Room

cards.title: R030 Group Study Room

cards.title: R060F Group Study Room
cards.subtitle: Raynor Library
cards.notes: Use this three-person room for a shared problem set or discussion, and add notes directly to its documented dry-erase board.
cards.short_summary: A reservable small-group room built around a dry-erase board.
cards.evidence_claim: Raynor lists R060F as a reservable group study room for at least three students with a dry erase board.
cards.source_title: Group Study Rooms | Raynor Library
cards.access_notes: Only enrolled Marquette undergraduates and graduate students may reserve rooms; a Marquette login may be required.

cards.title: R136 Group Study Room
cards.subtitle: Raynor Library

cards.access_notes: Only enrolled Marquette undergraduates and graduate students may reserve rooms; a Marquette login may be required.

cards.title: R165 Group Study Room
cards.subtitle: Raynor Library
cards.notes: Set up your group’s documents on the HDMI display, then use the dry-erase board to track decisions and next steps.

cards.evidence_claim: Raynor lists R165 as a reservable group study room for at least three students with a dry erase board and HDMI display.
cards.source_title: Group Study Rooms | Raynor Library
cards.access_notes: Only enrolled Marquette undergraduates and graduate students may reserve rooms; a Marquette login may be required.

cards.title: R221 Group Study Room
cards.subtitle: Raynor Library
cards.notes: Coordinate a larger group of five or more in R221, using its dry-erase board and HDMI display for a shared agenda.

cards.evidence_claim: Raynor lists R221 as a large reservable group study room for at least five students with a dry erase board and HDMI display.
cards.source_title: Group Study Rooms | Raynor Library

cards.title: Graduate Student Study Room (R134)

cards.evidence_claim: Raynor designates R134 for graduate students; it is nonreservable, MU ID-accessed, and has a dry erase board and HDMI display.
cards.source_title: Group Study Rooms | Raynor Library
cards.access_notes: Restricted to graduate students; enter by tapping an MU ID card on the reader near the door.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named destinations on corridors immediately west and east of Marquette’s urban campus, each with one concrete reason to stop.

cards.title: Pabst Mansion
cards.subtitle: W. Wisconsin Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk west on Wisconsin Avenue to see the preserved historic house museum; reserve a tour online if you want to go inside.
cards.short_summary: A historic-house stop with a documented visitor center and tours.
cards.evidence_claim: Pabst Mansion is a historic house museum at 2000 W. Wisconsin Ave. and offers tours with online reservations.
cards.source_title: The Pabst Mansion
cards.access_notes: Interior tours require admission; check the museum’s current tour availability before visiting.

cards.title: Ambassador Hotel Milwaukee
cards.subtitle: W. Wisconsin Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the Wisconsin Avenue walk to spot the Ambassador’s Art Deco façade and its clearly listed 2308 W. Wisconsin Avenue address.
cards.short_summary: An Art Deco hotel landmark along the westbound Wisconsin Avenue route.
cards.evidence_claim: Ambassador Hotel Milwaukee lists its location as 2308 W. Wisconsin Ave., Milwaukee.
cards.source_title: Ambassador Hotel Milwaukee — Contact Us
cards.access_notes: View the exterior from the public sidewalk; hotel services have their own access terms.

cards.title: Milwaukee Public Library Central Library
cards.subtitle: W. Wisconsin Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Head east on Wisconsin Avenue for Central Library and use its public collections, exhibits, or research resources during posted hours.
cards.short_summary: A city library destination on Wisconsin Avenue with public research resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Milwaukee Public Library identifies Central Library at 814 W. Wisconsin Avenue.
cards.source_title: Milwaukee Public Library
cards.access_notes: Confirm current branch hours and any event-specific requirements with Milwaukee Public Library.

cards.title: Milwaukee Public Museum
cards.subtitle: W. Wells Street corridor
cards.notes: Follow Wells Street toward the Milwaukee Public Museum for its science and history galleries; consult the museum before planning entry.
cards.short_summary: A museum stop on Wells Street for science and regional-history exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Milwaukee lists Milwaukee Public Museum at 800 W. Wells Street.
cards.source_title: City of Milwaukee — Researching Your Property
cards.access_notes: Museum admission and hours may vary; verify them directly before your visit.

cards.title: Milwaukee County Courthouse
cards.subtitle: N. 9th Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the N. 9th Street corridor to identify the courthouse at 901 N. 9th Street and its civic architecture from public areas.
cards.short_summary: A civic landmark on the eastward route from campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Milwaukee County lists the Register of Deeds at the County Courthouse, 901 N. 9th Street.
cards.source_title: Milwaukee County Register of Deeds — Real Estate Records
cards.access_notes: Government-building entry can involve security procedures and office-hour limits.

cards.title: Zeidler Municipal Building
cards.subtitle: N. Broadway corridor
cards.notes: Continue to N. Broadway to find the Zeidler Municipal Building, a city-government destination with historic-preservation offices inside.
cards.short_summary: A municipal landmark on the Broadway corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Milwaukee identifies the Zeidler Municipal Building at 841 N. Broadway and locates City Records and Historic Preservation offices there.
cards.source_title: City of Milwaukee — Researching Your Property
cards.access_notes: Access is governed by city office hours and building procedures.

cards.title: Milwaukee County Historical Society
cards.subtitle: N. Old World Third Street corridor
cards.notes: Take Old World Third Street to the Historical Society and plan ahead if you want to use its history materials or arrange a visit.
cards.short_summary: A local-history destination in a city-designated historic building.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Milwaukee identifies the Milwaukee County Historical Society Building at 910 N. Old World Third Street.
cards.source_title: City of Milwaukee — Historic Properties & Districts
cards.access_notes: Check the Historical Society directly for current public access and research-visit arrangements.

cards.title: Baird Center
cards.subtitle: N. Vel R. Phillips Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk the Vel R. Phillips Avenue corridor to Baird Center and check its public calendar for conventions, exhibitions, or community events.
cards.short_summary: A downtown convention-center destination with an event calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: Baird Center identifies its facility at 400 W. Wisconsin Avenue in downtown Milwaukee.
cards.source_title: Baird Center
cards.access_notes: Building access depends on scheduled events; review the organizer’s entry details before going.

cards.title: Fiserv Forum
cards.subtitle: N. Vel R. Phillips Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Continue north on Vel R. Phillips Avenue to Fiserv Forum and use the official event calendar to choose an age-appropriate program.
cards.short_summary: A major arena destination along the Vel R. Phillips Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Fiserv Forum lists its address as 1111 Vel R. Phillips Ave., Milwaukee.
cards.source_title: Fiserv Forum — Directions and Parking
cards.access_notes: Entry requires a ticket for most events; select an all-ages event and review its venue policies.

cards.title: Real Chili
cards.subtitle: W. Wells Street corridor
cards.notes: On Wells Street, stop at Real Chili for its documented chili, noodles, beans, and the Marquette special listed by the university.
cards.short_summary: A named Wells Street restaurant with a Marquette-specific menu item.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette University lists Real Chili at 1625 W. Wells St. and describes its chili, noodles, beans, and Marquette special.
cards.source_title: Marquette Today — Support on-campus retail partners this summer
cards.access_notes: Food purchases are required; confirm current ordering options and hours directly with the restaurant.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Marquette ceremonies, service practices and recurring campus rituals.

cards.title: New Student Convocation
cards.subtitle: Alumni Memorial Union · entering class welcome
cards.notes: Attend the entering-class gathering, where Marquette formally welcomes new students and introduces several campus rituals.
cards.short_summary: Marquette’s entering-class ceremony began in 1994.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette identifies New Student Convocation as an important tradition begun in 1994 and the first time the entering class gathers as a group.
cards.source_title: New Student Convocation
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of new-student programming; confirm the current program details with New Student and Family Programs.

cards.title: Meet the Honor Pledge
cards.subtitle: New Student Convocation · academic-community ritual
cards.notes: Listen for the Honor Pledge during Convocation and use the moment to understand one of the traditions introduced to newcomers.
cards.short_summary: The pledge is formally introduced with the incoming class.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette’s Convocation page lists the Honor Pledge among the key university traditions introduced during New Student Convocation.
cards.source_title: New Student Convocation
cards.access_notes: Presented within New Student Convocation; participation details are set by the program.

cards.title: Mission the Incoming Class
cards.subtitle: New Student Convocation · class welcome ritual
cards.notes: Notice the Missioning of the incoming class at Convocation, a named ritual that marks students’ entrance into the university community.
cards.short_summary: A formal ritual for the new class’s entry into Marquette.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette’s Convocation page names the Missioning of the incoming class as a key university tradition introduced at the ceremony.
cards.source_title: New Student Convocation
cards.access_notes: Presented within New Student Convocation; check the current Convocation program for timing.

cards.title: Learn the University Fight Song
cards.subtitle: New Student Convocation · shared school-spirit ritual
cards.notes: Learn the University Fight Song when it is introduced at Convocation, then recognize it at future Marquette community gatherings.
cards.short_summary: The fight song is one of Convocation’s named tradition introductions.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette lists the University Fight Song among the key university traditions introduced at New Student Convocation.
cards.source_title: New Student Convocation
cards.access_notes: Introduced during New Student Convocation; subsequent appearances vary by event.

cards.title: Start the Year at Mass of the Holy Spirit
cards.subtitle: Church of the Gesu · academic-year gathering
cards.notes: Join the university-wide Mass and follow the gathering with the listed community picnic when the annual program is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: A Jesuit academic tradition that opens the year in shared reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette describes its Mass of the Holy Spirit as part of a Jesuit academic tradition dating to 1548; its 2026 gathering is scheduled at the Church of the Gesu.
cards.source_title: Mass of the Holy Spirit
cards.access_notes: The university lists the 2026 Mass for Aug. 30 at 6 p.m.; all are welcome. Confirm future dates before attending.

cards.entity_name: Tuesday Night Mass at St. Joan of Arc Chapel
cards.title: Tuesday Night Mass in the Chapel
cards.subtitle: St. Joan of Arc Chapel · student-led weekly Mass
cards.notes: Visit the historic chapel for the student-led Tuesday-night Mass, a Marquette tradition documented in the university’s Commencement Series.
cards.short_summary: A student-led Mass tradition in Marquette’s historic chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette Today calls Tuesday night Mass at St. Joan of Arc Chapel a classic Marquette tradition and describes it as student-led.
cards.source_title: 2026 Commencement Series: Chance meeting leads to student receiving three sacraments just before graduation
cards.access_notes: Campus Ministry schedules student Masses; verify the current time and chapel access before going.

cards.title: Have Soup with Substance
cards.subtitle: Alumni Memorial Union · Wednesday social-justice conversation
cards.notes: Bring your attention to a social-justice issue over soup and bread at this longstanding Wednesday-noon Campus Ministry tradition.
cards.short_summary: A weekly simple meal paired with discussion and a presentation.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Ministry calls Soup with Substance a longstanding tradition held every Wednesday at noon in the Alumni Memorial Union, with soup, bread and social-justice conversation.
cards.source_title: Get Involved with Campus Ministry
cards.access_notes: Listed for Wednesdays at noon in the Alumni Memorial Union; confirm dates and availability with Campus Ministry.

cards.title: Join the Midnight Run
cards.subtitle: Campus Ministry · weekly Milwaukee service
cards.notes: Sign up with a service site and return weekly with your team to support meal programs, pantries, shelters and other partners.
cards.short_summary: A student-organized weekly service practice dating to 1988.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette says Midnight Run began as a student response to community need in 1988 and sends weekly volunteers to Milwaukee service sites.
cards.source_title: Midnight Run
cards.access_notes: Participation requires signing up through Campus Ministry; service-site schedules and requirements vary.

cards.title: Take Part in Community Day of Service
cards.subtitle: Milwaukee partner agencies · annual service day
cards.notes: Register with a volunteer team for the spring service day and work alongside local agencies in intentional community engagement.
cards.short_summary: Marquette’s largest and longest-running day of service.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arrupe Center identifies Marquette Community Day of Service, formerly Hunger Clean-Up, as the university’s largest and longest-running day of service.
cards.source_title: Marquette Community Day of Service
cards.access_notes: Held annually; registration, partner locations and transportation details are announced for each year’s program.

cards.title: Gather for the Tree Lighting
cards.subtitle: Westowne Square · annual December ceremony
cards.notes: Gather in Westowne Square for carols, remarks and the lighting of Marquette’s permanent annual Christmas tree.
cards.short_summary: A campus December ceremony with the Pep Band and All-Campus Choir.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette reports that its annual Christmas tree lighting returned to Westowne Square in 2025, with carols, presidential remarks and a tree blessing.
cards.source_title: Marquette community gathers for annual Christmas tree lighting
cards.access_notes: An annual early-December event; watch Marquette Today for the current date and location.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Marquette University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe first-weekend loop through Marquette’s campus spaces: get oriented, find practical resources, and leave room for a museum or performance.

cards.title: Start at the Alumni Memorial Union
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · 1442 W. Wisconsin Ave.
cards.notes: Use the union as your first indoor landmark: check the building directory, locate campus services, and choose one later stop before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A practical first anchor for getting oriented on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette identifies the Alumni Memorial Union as its student union and a gathering place for campus activities, dining, studying, and meeting others.
cards.source_title: Alumni Memorial Union
cards.access_notes: Building access and hours can change; consult the AMU site before visiting.

cards.title: Make a quick Brew Bayou stop
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · AMU first floor
cards.notes: If you want a drink or snack while orienting yourself, find Brew Bayou just off the AMU’s main east entrance; skip it if you are not buying.
cards.short_summary: An optional coffee-shop pause inside the union.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette’s AMU facilities overview lists Brew Bayou coffee shop directly off the building’s main east entrance.
cards.source_title: Alumni Memorial Union Facilities Overview
cards.access_notes: Purchase is optional; verify current café hours on arrival.

cards.title: Learn the route to Raynor Library
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · 1355 W. Wisconsin Ave.
cards.notes: Walk through Raynor before classes begin and note its accessible entrances, study areas, computers, loanable laptops, and research-help options.
cards.short_summary: A first-weekend reconnaissance stop for academic routines.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette states that Raynor Memorial Libraries provides study and group-study spaces, computer access, laptops on loan, research databases, and research staff.
cards.source_title: Raynor Library
cards.access_notes: The official campus-map page lists wheelchair-accessible entrances at the northwest and southwest doors.

cards.title: Pause at St. Joan of Arc Chapel
cards.subtitle: Friday late afternoon · south side of campus
cards.notes: Take a quiet exterior-and-interior visit if open, then use the chapel’s location west of Raynor as a waypoint for the south side of campus.
cards.short_summary: A contemplative historic stop near the libraries.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette’s visitor information places St. Joan of Arc Chapel on the south side of campus, west of the Raynor Memorial Libraries.
cards.source_title: Visiting St. Joan of Arc Chapel
cards.access_notes: Check the chapel’s visitor information for current opening and worship schedules before entering.

cards.title: See what is on view at Haggerty
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · campus museum visit
cards.notes: Choose one current exhibition or program and give it unhurried time; the museum is a useful rainy-day option during your first campus weekend.
cards.short_summary: A free, public-facing art stop on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Haggerty Museum of Art states that its exhibitions and programs are free and open to the public unless otherwise noted.
cards.source_title: Haggerty Museum of Art Hours of Operation
cards.access_notes: Confirm exhibition hours and any exception noted by the museum before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Lalumiere Language Hall Outdoor Workout Stations
cards.title: Try the Lalumiere outdoor stations
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · beside Lalumiere Language Hall
cards.notes: Take a short movement break using the skill trainer, body-curl station, or plyometric boxes, choosing a pace and exercise that feels comfortable.
cards.short_summary: A simple outdoor activity embedded in a campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette’s employee-wellness page documents a skill trainer, body-curl station, and plyometric boxes at Lalumiere Language Hall.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Workout Stations
cards.access_notes: Use the stations as intended and adapt or skip movements that do not feel safe or accessible.

cards.title: Find Brooks Lounge for a reset
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · AMU first floor
cards.notes: Return to the AMU and locate Brooks Lounge so you know a named indoor spot with pool tables and space to sit, study, or decompress.
cards.short_summary: An easy indoor regrouping point in the union.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette’s AMU facilities overview describes Brooks Lounge as having pool tables and hangout/study space.
cards.source_title: Alumni Memorial Union Facilities Overview
cards.access_notes: Located on the AMU first floor; access is subject to building hours and scheduled use.

cards.title: Locate the Chapel of the Holy Family
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · AMU second floor
cards.notes: While you are in the union, find this second-floor chapel and the nearby prayer and meditation spaces for a future quiet pause between activities.
cards.short_summary: A named quiet-space landmark inside the AMU.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette lists the Chapel of the Holy Family on the AMU second floor near the Interfaith Prayer and Meditation Space and Muslim Prayer Space.
cards.source_title: Alumni Memorial Union Facilities Overview
cards.access_notes: Respect active services and posted access guidance; availability may vary with campus programming.

cards.title: Check the Varsity Theatre calendar
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · Holthusen Hall, 1326 W. Wisconsin Ave.
cards.notes: Walk by the theatre and look for a suitable upcoming concert, movie, or campus performance; choose a ticketed event only after checking its age policy.
cards.short_summary: A campus venue to keep in mind for a future evening.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette describes Varsity Theatre in Holthusen Hall as a venue for national music acts, movies, and Marquette band, choir, and orchestra concerts.
cards.source_title: Marquette Wayfinder
cards.access_notes: Programming, tickets, and age policies vary by event; verify details with the event organizer before attending.

cards.title: End by finding Weasler Auditorium
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · Alumni Memorial Union complex
cards.notes: Add Weasler to your mental map for future plays, speakers, or dance practice, then head home with the key campus landmarks already familiar.
cards.short_summary: A final campus-performance landmark for the weekend loop.
cards.evidence_claim: Marquette describes Weasler Auditorium as a full-service theater with a built-in audio system, dressing rooms, and stage that can be used for plays, speakers, or dance practice.
cards.source_title: Alumni Memorial Union Facilities Overview
cards.access_notes: Event access, timing, and ticket requirements depend on the scheduled program.
